4.text: Quarrels between father and sons occur every now and then. In this

5.text: case the family ties may be broken by, either party. Thus, on the Dry Anui

6.text: River, one of my acquaintances, Kelhɪˊm by name, expelled from his camp

7.text: his son Kɪʟeˊp, a young man of twenty, accusing him of laziness, bad temper,

8.text: and neglect of his duties as a herdsman. The young man, according to the

9.text: words of his father, wanted to attend friendly gatherings, to play cards, and

10.text: to make merry. The father declared that he himself was entitled to these

11.text: privileges, insisting that it was the duty of young men to take care of the

12.text: reindeer-herd. Kɪʟeˊp left his father’s camp, and wandered around, trying to

13.text: find a place in some family as an adopted son-in-law; but the work required

14.text: in such positions seemed to be much harder than that required in his father’s

15.text: house, and at last he returned home. His father was short of herdsmen, and

16.text: the young man was re-admitted without much difficulty. After a few weeks,

17.text: however, misunderstandings began anew. We visited the camp of Kelhɪˊm

18.text: about that time. One night the young man came home from the herd, ripped
